items.title:
Daily Ukraine map thread for Sunday 25th October 2026

A quick look at the rear areas over the past couple of weeks, because while Ukrainian strikes inside Russia rightly attract attention, it's worth looking at what Russia is doing to Ukraine in return.

Epicenter stores, long a favourite Russian target, have been wiped out across much of Ukraine. As we update the map, more geolocations have come in of further stores struck and burning in Zaporizhzhia and Poltava. Ukrainian air defences simply cannot intercept everything, particularly as Russian production continues to grow.

Ukraine is hitting back, but the comparison is stark. Drones can reach deep into Russia, but against hardened industrial facilities, they have limitations. Fortunately, a delivery of British-French Storm Shadow missiles has given Ukraine some heavier options this weekend.

The Proton semiconductor plant in Oryol and the Energiya plant in Yelets have both been struck by Storm Shadows, inflicting significant damage. These are precisely the sort of targets where a heavier missile can achieve effects that drones struggle to replicate.

Meanwhile, at the front, Russian forces continue to advance, but at a crawl. The territorial gains remain painfully slow and come at enormous human cost. Both sides seem quite content with what they are achieving, however the 'magical' maps that Russia has constructed of it's own advances doesn't adhere to reality on the ground.

So yes, Ukrainian strikes inside Russia are important. But look at the bigger picture please, and we'll leave the rest unsaid.
